humanities_role_explanation: Evaluates automated subject indexing and library cataloging, which is a disciplinary competency within Library Science and Museology, utilizing the German Integrated Authority File (GND) taxonomy.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Evaluates using text-only bibliographic metadata consisting of record titles and abstracts in English and German.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Extreme multi-label text classification (XMTC) to assign and rank relevant subject headings from a large-scale controlled vocabulary taxonomy (GND) for library records.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped specifically to the task of automated subject tagging and cataloging in libraries.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates various generative models such as GPT-4o, Llama-3.1, Llama-3.2, Qwen2.5, ChatGLM 4, and Mistral.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluated using Precision@k, Recall@k, and F1-score@k, complemented by qualitative expert evaluation from subject specialists.

published_after_march_2023.note: Published as a SemEval-2025 task preprint in May 2025.

summary: This paper introduces SemEval-2025 Task 5: LLMs4Subjects, a shared task evaluating large language models for automated bilingual subject tagging of scientific and technical library records using the GND taxonomy. It establishes a benchmark on German and English catalog records and presents both quantitative metrics and professional human evaluations of participating systems.
key_findings: The top-performing systems quantitatively combined traditional extreme multi-label classification tools with LLM-assisted translation, synthetic data generation, or cross-lingual embeddings (Annif, RUC Team, and DUTIR831). In qualitative evaluations by subject librarians, a zero-shot/few-shot prompted LLM ensemble (DNB-AI-Project) achieved the highest precision and recall scores without fine-tuning, demonstrating the strong generalization capabilities of LLMs.
facets_explanation: The reference subject tags were extracted from existing library metadata in the TIBKAT catalog, which are assigned by specialized librarians using the German National Library's GND taxonomy. Correctly identifying these subjects requires knowledge of this taxonomy and its conceptual linkages, which are external to the provided title and abstract. Performance is evaluated quantitatively against a set of multiple pre-existing subject tags using precision and recall at k, and the paper does not address annotator divergence in the gold standard creation.
